title: Serge Belamant
text:
South African entrepreneur (born 1953)

| Serge Christian Pierre Belamant | |
| --- | --- |
| Born | (1953-09-22) September 22, 1953 (age 72)  Tulle, France |
| Occupations | Entrepreneur, inventor |
| Known for | Universal Electronic Payment System (UEPS); Chip Offline Pre-authorised Card (COPAC) |
| Title | Founder of Net1 UEPS Technologies; Co-founder & chair of Zilch |

**Serge Belamant** (born 1953) is a French-born South African entrepreneur best known for designing the Universal Electronic [Payment System](/wiki/Payment_system "Payment system") (UEPS) and the Chip Offline Pre-authorised Card (COPAC).[[1]](#cite_note-:0-1)[[2]](#cite_note-2)

He founded the cash-payments company Net1 UEPS Technologies in 1989, led it through dual listings on the [NASDAQ](/wiki/NASDAQ "NASDAQ") and the [Johannesburg Stock Exchange](/wiki/Johannesburg_Stock_Exchange "Johannesburg Stock Exchange"), and oversaw the contentious welfare-payments contract with the South African Social Security Agency (SASSA) until his retirement in 2017.[[3]](#cite_note-3) Since 2018 he has been non-executive chair of London-based buy-now-pay-later fintech Zilch.[[1]](#cite_note-:0-1)

title: Serge Belamant
text:
## Early life and education

Belamant moved from France to South Africa with his family in 1967 and matriculated from Highlands North Boys' High School, Johannesburg.[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] In 1972 he entered the [University of the Witwatersrand](/wiki/University_of_the_Witwatersrand "University of the Witwatersrand") to study civil engineering but switched to computer science and [applied mathematics](/wiki/Applied_mathematics "Applied mathematics") in his second year. He left the university without a degree and later took short courses in information systems at the [University of South Africa](/wiki/University_of_South_Africa "University of South Africa") (UNISA).[[4]](#cite_note-4)

title: Serge Belamant
text:
## Early career and SASWITCH (1981–1989)

Belamant worked for [Control Data Corporation](/wiki/Control_Data_Corporation "Control Data Corporation") as a systems analyst for a decade before joining SASWITCH Ltd in 1985.[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] Economic sanctions had left the consortium's national ATM network dependent on unsupported Christian Rovsing computers.[[5]](#cite_note-BizNewsInterview-5) Belamant led a rebuild on fault-tolerant Stratus hardware and wrote protocol-translation software that allowed fourteen banks to connect without altering their host systems.[[6]](#cite_note-CompCom2008-6)

By 1988 SASWITCH was handling about three million ATM transactions a month, according to the Competition Commission.[[5]](#cite_note-BizNewsInterview-5) The switch—now run by BankservAfrica—remains the backbone of South Africa's shared ATM network.[[7]](#cite_note-:2-7)

title: Serge Belamant
text:
### Founding and UEPS

In 1989, Serge Belamant developed the Universal Electronic Payment System (UEPS), enabling secure, real-time transactions even in areas with limited connectivity. In the same year, he founded NET1 UEPS Technologies Inc., serving as its CEO and Director.[[7]](#cite_note-:2-7)

title: Serge Belamant
text:
### COPAC for VISA

In 1995, VISA tasked Belamant with designing the Chip Offline Pre-authorized Card (COPAC), a technology still widely used in chip-enabled credit and debit cards.[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] A year later, he listed his company APLITEC (Applied Technology Holdings Limited) on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

title: Serge Belamant
text:
### Listings and acquisitions

In 1999, Belamant acquired Cash Payment Services (CPS) from First National Bank of South Africa, modernizing its welfare payment system to serve millions in rural areas.[[9]](#cite_note-9) In 2005, he led NET1 Technologies to an IPO, listing it as NET1 UEPS Technologies Inc. on the Nasdaq. A secondary listing on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) followed in 2008.[[10]](#cite_note-10)

title: Serge Belamant
text:
### SASSA contract

Under Belamant's leadership, NET1 managed welfare payments for the South African Social Security Agency (SASSA), handling payments for over 10 million beneficiaries monthly.[[11]](#cite_note-11) Despite criticism over handling the SASSA contract, investigations by the [U.S. Department of Justice](/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Justice "United States Department of Justice") and the South African Constitutional Court found no wrongdoing.[[12]](#cite_note-12)

title: Serge Belamant
text:
## Zilch (2018–present)

Belamant co-founded London-based "buy-now-pay-later" firm Zilch Technology in 2018 and serves as non-executive chair.[[1]](#cite_note-:0-1) Zilch reported £145 million in annual-recurring revenue and 4.5 million customers in January 2025.[[13]](#cite_note-13)

title: Serge Belamant
text:
## Patents

Belamant is listed as inventor on more than a dozen payment-security patents, including:

- "Funds transfer system" (US RE36,788, 2000) – the basis for UEPS.[[14]](#cite_note-14)
- "Financial transactions with a varying PIN" (WO 2014/037869, 2014).[[15]](#cite_note-15)
